origin.description: Modifies a date-time object by adding a specific amount of time units.
origin.usage: stri_datetime_add(time, value = 1L, units = "seconds", tz = NULL, locale = NULL)

arguments.name: time
arguments.text: A POSIXct, or a character, Date, POSIXlt, or factor value coerced with as.POSIXct.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Integer vector. Signed number of units to add.

arguments.name: units
arguments.text: One of years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, or milliseconds. A unique prefix is enough.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default time zone, or one ICU time zone identifier.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects a calendar.

origin.details: Vectorized over time and value. Adding a day keeps the local time of day. Adding 24 hours can cross a daylight-saving change. January 31 plus one month is February 28 or 29.
origin.example:
x <- stri_datetime_add(stri_datetime_create(2024, 1, 31, tz = "UTC"), 1, units = "months", tz = "UTC")
cat(paste0("stri_datetime_add of 2024-01-31 plus one month returns ", sprintf("%.0f", unclass(x)), ".\n"))

translation.description: Adds calendar units to each instant.

arguments.name: time
arguments.text: Seconds since the epoch, a date-time string in one of the six as.POSIXct formats, NA, or a list of one kind.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: An int or a list of ints. A fractional number is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: units
arguments.text: A unique prefix of years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, or milliseconds.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: None or "" for the default ICU zone, or one zone identifier.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects a calendar.

translation.details: A character time is parsed in the default zone, the same way as.POSIXct parses it. Adding a day keeps the local clock time. Adding 24 hours follows elapsed time and can land on a different clock time after a daylight-saving change. A missing instant or a missing value stays missing.
translation.value: A float, or NA. A list or tuple returns a list.
translation.example:
from stringi.datetime import stri_datetime_add, stri_datetime_create
x = stri_datetime_add(stri_datetime_create(2024, 1, 31, tz="UTC"), 1, units="months", tz="UTC")
print(f"stri_datetime_add of 2024-01-31 plus one month returns {x:.0f}.")
